item.title: Brazil launches probe into alleged Trump administration plan to fund far-right causes in the country
item.description: The investigation comes as both Lula and Flavio Bolsonaro prepare to contest each other for what is being described as a consequential election in Brazil, that could shape the developing economy’s forecast and future for decades to come.

item.title: Unamuno and H. G. Wells went to the cinema together: unpublished letter confirms it 90 years on
item.description: Written in 1936 and found in the archive of Salamanca’s Casa-Museo Unamuno, the document confirms the Spanish writer dined with the author of 'The War of the Worlds' before going to the cinema together in London.

item.title: Danish military admits flaws in report about 2025 drone incursions
item.description: In a revised report of the incident at Skrydstrup air base released Thursday, the military admitted that their account might have been mistaken.

item.title: Manchester City not 'above the rules', says Downing Street
item.description: After PM Andy Burnham's - a former mayor of Greater Manchester - admission of his fears that the club's owners might leave because of the investigation into 'creative book-keeping', his spokesperson has issued a clarification.

item.title: Kyrylo Budanov: European security without the US would be ‘very dangerous’
item.description: In an exclusive interview with Euronews, the head of the Ukrainian President's Office warned against a future European security architecture without the US and outlined Kyiv’s vision for deeper defence cooperation with Europe.

item.title: José Sevilla resigns as Unicaja chair and declines to remain at the bank
item.description: José Sevilla will step down as Unicaja chairman in April 2027 after deciding not to seek a new term, but will retain his non-executive role at the Málaga-based bank until then.

item.title: France: Media outlet publishes new antisemitic screenshots attributed to Jordan Bardella
item.description: In a second wave of revelations around Jordan Bardella, investigative outlet Mediapart has published new screenshots of antisemitic messages attributed to the RN leader, who denies writing them.

item.title: Europe went all in on soft power for too long, Belgian defence minister says
item.description: In an interview with Euronews, the Belgian defence minister argued that Europe spent too long focusing on soft power instead of defence.

item.title: French protests over school conditions spread as students set fires and put up blockades
item.description: High school students were joined on Thursday by university students, as violent incidents took place in several French cities and even spread to the Belgian city of Liege.

item.title: Palermo, first coffee grown and harvested in Italy: warmer climate is changing farming
item.description: Rising temperatures now allow coffee to be grown in Italy. In Sicily, the Morettino family has completed its first harvest, showing how climate change is reshaping crops worldwide.

item.title: Uzbekistan’s rich cultural heritage on display in Qatar
item.description: Qatar’s Museum of Islamic Art spotlights Uzbekistan’s rich cultural heritage. We meet the curator of ‘Uzbekistan: Heritage in Motion’ to learn about centuries of Islamic art, craftsmanship and traditions.

item.title: Elon Musk returns to Trump administration to co-lead Pentagon war study
item.description: Musk, who in 2024 threw his support behind Trump and helped his return to the White House, served as head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), where he spearheaded sweeping job cuts across the US federal government.

item.title: El representante de EE.UU. en la OTAN: La revisión de las tropas en Europa dependerá del "América primero"
item.description: The review of troops stationed in Europe was initiated after tensions rose over some NATO countries refusing US troops access to military bases for use in the war in Iran.

item.title: 'Don't care about supporting Russia': Bulgarian PM hits back against pro-Moscow label
item.description: The Bulgarian prime minister is principal among EU leaders calling for talks with Moscow over its war on Ukraine, earning him a pro-Russia label.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 1st, 2026 – Evening
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 1st, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Woody Allen presents new film in Madrid, funded with €3m in public money
item.description: The 90-year-old American director has unveiled in the capital his 51st film, due to start shooting on 5 October with public funding, as past scandals still shadow his career.

item.title: Greece pitches suspension of the EU’s right to asylum during migration crises
item.description: A special regime would be activated in case of a rapid increase in arrivals and migrants flows used as a hybrid threat by third countries. Several EU governments seem open to the proposal, which could feature in the Commission’s new Emergency Response.

item.title: Greece to set up a new national dementia centre for patients, families and caretakers
item.description: The new centre in Athens will provide cognitive training, occupational and music therapy, plus services for prevention, diagnosis and ongoing patient monitoring.

item.title: ‘Releasing strategic reserves is a possibility,’ EU energy chief tells Euronews as diesel squeeze bites
item.description: Member states are discussing a coordinated release through the IEA, as the US pressures Europe to put more oil on the market. The Energy Commissioner told Euronews that Brussels can help coordinate the effort.

item.title: WATCH: NATO model 'not sustainable', alliance's chief Mark Rutte tells Euronews
item.description: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte spoke exclusively to Euronews about the most pressing challenges facing the alliance, including overreliance on the US and Russia's nuclear threat. Watch the interview here.

item.title: EU turns page on Ukraine's $27 billion deficit, says all needs are covered
item.description: The mystery surrounding Ukraine's $27 billion shortfall abruptly ended on Thursday as the European Commission confirmed the country's financial and military needs for 2026 are fully covered.

item.title: ‘Set-jetting’ trips: How to holiday like the Gilmore Girls in Stars Hollow
item.description: From the fictional Connecticut town of Gilmore Girls' Stars Hollow to destinations closer to home in Europe, the set-jetting trend continues to turn film and TV locations into travel experiences.

item.title: Alliance against invisibility: Prado and Rijksmuseum join forces for women in art
item.description: Madrid's Prado Museum and Amsterdam's Rijksmuseum are joining forces in a strategic alliance to explore women's role in history and reassess the shared heritage between Spain and the Netherlands.

item.title: Russia expels Hungarian diplomats as Budapest breaks with Orbán era
item.description: Moscow ordered Hungarian embassy and consulate staff out just weeks after Budapest expelled 10 Russian diplomats on national security grounds in September, the first such move by Hungary since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

item.title: Shakira and Amazon Music stream Madrid concert live and free
item.description: Shakira will livestream a full concert worldwide for the first time. The show, broadcast free from Madrid on 3 October, will be available via Amazon Music, Prime Video and Twitch.

item.title: No relief at the pump: EU diesel hits new record of €2.24 a litre
item.description: Twelve EU countries recorded new diesel price highs as supply disruptions pushed the bloc’s average pump price to €2.24 a litre.

item.title: Young martial artists train in China’s ancient mountain schools
item.description: Young students from China and abroad train in tai chi and kung fu on the Wudang Mountains, where Taoist philosophy shapes martial arts and daily life.

item.title: Finland investigates suspected break-ins at several MPs homes, authorities say
item.description: All members of parliament had been told to remain vigilant, report observations and file police complaints if necessary.

item.title: EU watchdogs question Binance over unlicensed European operations
item.description: European regulators are questioning Binance over its use of a narrow legal exemption to keep serving EU customers without a licence, the Financial Times reported. Binance told Euronews it is working towards authorisation, while ESMA said enforcement is a matter for national authorities.

item.title: Can Europe afford its defence boost? MEPs debate in The Ring
item.description: As security and hybrid threats are on the rise across Europe and the war in Ukraine enters its fifth year, the focus in Brussels is firmly on increasing defence spending. But who should pay, and how?

item.title: Gaza documentary ‘NAZA’ beating ‘Avengers Endgame: Encore’ at box office
item.description: 'NAZA', the award-winning documentary which examines "the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians", is currently beating the recently re-released Marvel film ‘Avengers Endgame: Encore’ at the Italian box office. The documentary is set to be released globally this month.

item.title: Portugal records biggest EU rise in house prices in second quarter
item.description: Eurostat data shows Portugal recorded the EU's sharpest rise in house prices in Q2 2026 versus a year earlier. In September, national housing costs hit a fresh record high.

item.title: Barcelona-Amsterdam: Europe's most stressful air route for nervous flyers
item.description: The route between Barcelona El Prat and Amsterdam Schiphol tops a ranking that also lists Madrid-London Heathrow in 10th place, according to AirAdvisor.

item.title: Falling numbers: Thymaina's plunging population shows Greece's demographic decline
item.description: Desertification in rural areas and on the islands is forcing schools to shut. On a small eastern Aegean island, locals speak of soaring costs, isolation and a future without children.

item.title: Rogue AI agents tried and failed to hack US and Canadian government websites
item.description: Researchers cannot confidently say who was responsible, but evidence points to rogue Google and OpenAI agents carrying out a range of aggressive tactics to collect datasets and test their vulnerabilities.

item.title: Bradley Whitford receives Hollywood Walk of Fame star
item.description: Bradley Whitford receives the 2,858th star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame, celebrating with family and West Wing co-stars in Los Angeles.

item.title: Euronews Culture's Film of the Week: 'Digger' – Tom Cruise stuck in postmodernist misfire
item.description: Oscar-winning director Alejandro González Iñárritu teams up with Tom Cruise for 'Digger', one of the boldest and wildest films of 2026. It may also be one of this year's biggest misfires.

item.title: The rise of ‘micro-travel’ and other trends set to hit the big time in 2027, according to Hilton
item.description: Next year, travellers will be taking more frequent, but shorter, trips, booking onto 'growth getaways' and prioritising spending time in nature for wellness purposes.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 1st, 2026 – Midday
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 1st, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: 'They should cast Jack': Danny Boyle names his pick for the next James Bond
item.description: Jack O’Connell’s name has been mentioned as a possible Bond contender during the audition process, but has not been elevated to frontrunner status like Jack Lowden, Callum Turner, Jacob Elordi and Jack Barton. Now, ex-Bond director Danny Boyle has named O'Connell as his ideal pick for the new 007.

item.title: Trump announces $200bn in South Korean energy investment plans
item.description: US President Donald Trump announced Wednesday plans for $200 billion in South Korean investments in US energy projects, including $54 billion for a long-planned liquefied natural gas (LNG) project in Alaska that Seoul said it had not yet agreed to invest in.

item.title: Greece urges EU to loosen fiscal rules as energy crisis deepens
item.description: High energy prices and military escalation at energy facilities in the Middle East prompted Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis to ask Brussels for greater fiscal flexibility. Greece has the largest debt among EU countries and is heading to polls in 2027.

item.title: Several regions of Ukraine hit by power cuts after Russian strikes, grid operator says
item.description: Kyiv said it was Moscow's opening salvo in an expected campaign to try to knock out heating and power as winter approaches.

item.title: Four sailors rescued after sperm whale sinks yacht in South Pacific
item.description: Four sailors were rescued after a sperm whale struck and sank their yacht in the remote South Pacific. A New Zealand Air Force surveillance aircraft helped coordinate the rescue. The crew were taken aboard a cargo ship as their yacht went under.

item.title: ‘Thrilling’: Dutch cattle farmers switch to rice as solution to warmer climate and sinking peatlands
item.description: Dutch cattle farming dries out peatland and releases CO2. Is switching to Japanese rice-growing a solution?

item.title: Lost in translation: Montenegro's EU accession faces a language barrier
item.description: Montenegro may not be able to accurately translate all EU laws in time for accession, so the European Commission is currently weighing options for a derogation, including allowing Podgorica to use an existing EU language to fill the gaps. Croatian would be the most obvious choice.

item.title: PM Netanyahu says Israel warned UK of suspected Iran attack plot on RAF airbase
item.description: After three days of investigations, including using a bomb disposal team, police said on Tuesday they had found no explosives in the vehicles, but they had retrieved a "quantity of petrol."

item.title: Oil hovers around $100 as US bonds suffer their worst quarter since 1994
item.description: Oil prices bounced back above $100 a barrel on Thursday as a US-Iran deal remained elusive, while European stocks fell and US government bonds came off their worst quarter since 1994, with the 10-year Treasury yield at its highest since 2007.

item.title: France's borrowing rate keeps rising, hitting its highest level since 2002
item.description: The new rise in France's ten-year borrowing rate, now close to 5%, shows investors' mounting distrust of a public debt that keeps climbing.

item.title: Is the EU planning to freeze funds to German states that voted for the AfD?
item.description: Claims circulating online allege that the EU is threatening to block funds intended for the German state of Saxony-Anhalt, after the far-right AfD party won a recent election there. However, there's no evidence that this is the case.
